subject: Private deployment: credit escape & SLA tiering
messages:
From: Amber Holt <amber.holt@medtechcorp.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Darren Shaw <darren.shaw@medtechcorp.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment: credit escape & SLA tiering

Karthik / team,

Thanks for sending the initial commercial. A few procurement must-haves came back from our side after internal review:

- We need an explicit ‘escape hatch’ credit if we terminate within the first 18 months. Our finance policy typically requires a 25% credit on unamortized platform fees; can Redwood accommodate a negotiated percentage?
- SLA tiers must include a documented remediation credit table (P1/P2/P3) and a committed on-call response window for enterprise deployments.
- On support tiers: we want an option for an engineering retainer for first 6 months to cover runbook handoffs and troubleshooting, priced as a separate line item.

I attached our standard procurement questionnaire for reference. Please send a redline-friendly SOW and an amortization example that shows how platform fees would be applied over a 3-year term and under a 24-month early-termination scenario.

Thanks,
Amber
Amber Holt
Head of Cloud Ops, MedTech Corp
Attachment: MedTech_Procurement_Questionnaire.docx (DOCX, 120KB)
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Amber Holt <amber.holt@medtechcorp.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, rachel_kim@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment: credit escape & SLA tiering

Amber — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers and next steps below; happy to hop on a call to walk through numbers.

- Escape hatch credit: we can offer a tiered credit schedule rather than a flat percent. Example proposal: 0–6 months = 50% credit of remaining pre-paid platform fee, 6–18 months = 30%, 18–24 months = 15%. This preserves customer flexibility while protecting platform amortization.
- SLA remediation credits: we have a standard table (P1 = 10% credit per hour after SLA breach, capped at X% per incident) — I’ll include the explicit remediation schedule in the SOW.
- Engineering retainer: we can show a separate line for a 6-month retainer (40 hours/month of engineering support) as an optional add-on.

I’m attaching a pricing workbook with an amortization tab and two model scenarios (3-year amortization vs 24-month early termination) so you can see the math. Please confirm your expected monthly token/throughput profile so we can recommend whether to lean on reserved capacity (Dedicated) vs a VPC-bundled model.

Plan: I’ll drop an editable SOW draft with the remediation table and the tiered credit schedule by Friday. If procurement needs an alternate credit schedule, let me know ranges you’d consider.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
VP, Sales (Private Deployments)
Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_vpc_pricing_0519.xlsx (XLSX, 86KB)
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Amber Holt <amber.holt@medtechcorp.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 5 Jun 2026 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment: credit escape & SLA tiering

Amber — looping in Vivek who owns our Dedicated economics and support packaging.

Attached is an editable SOW (SOW_draft_v3.pdf) and a short pricing summary with 3 constructs:

1) Consumption-first VPC bundle: low upfront platform fee, higher per-node consumption, no dedicated engineering retainer included.
2) Amortized platform-fee model (recommended for predictable budgets): upfront platform fee amortized over 3 years with the tiered escape-credit schedule Karthik proposed.
3) Reserved Dedicated + reduced platform fee: higher commit on GPU capacity, lower platform fee and lower per-token cost; includes optional 6-month engineering retainer at discounted hourly rates.

SLA table highlights: P1/P2/P3 definitions, target MTTR, and explicit credit calculation examples. I added a sample amortization table for a $450k platform fee across 36 months and outlined the residual credit under each termination band.

Next steps: if Procurement confirms an acceptable escape-credit band (e.g., 30% at 6–18m), we can turn the SOW into a redline and route to Legal.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Head of Commercial Contracts, Redwood Inference
Attachment: SOW_draft_v3.pdf (PDF, 248KB)
From: Amber Holt <amber.holt@medtechcorp.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: MedTech Procurement <procurement@medtechcorp.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment: credit escape & SLA tiering

Thanks Laura/Karthik — the constructs are helpful. A few clarifications from Procurement:

- Procurement is pushing back on 50% in 0–6 months; they want a maximum of 40% in year one and would prefer a 25% cap in months 7–18. Are those ranges manageable?
- They require the remediation credit cap to be expressed as a percentage of the platform fee and a separate percentage of monthly managed services charges.
- For the engineering retainer, procurement needs a fixed-price option (not hourly) for budget predictability. Can you provide a 6-month fixed retainer price?

Procurement has requested the SOW and pricing workbook in tracked-change Word/PDF and a short note that this commercial will be honored through 30 Jun 2026 so they can align internal approvals.

Amber

--
Amber Holt
Head of Cloud Ops, MedTech Corp
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Amber Holt <amber.holt@medtechcorp.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, rachel_kim@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2026 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment: credit escape & SLA tiering

Amber — appreciate the specifics. We can meet Procurement halfway: proposed final commercial terms below. I’m available for a 30-min sync this week if you want to finalize before the end-of-month hold.

Proposed changes:
- Escape hatch credit (final): 0–6 months = 40% credit of remaining pre-paid platform fee; 6–18 months = 25%; 18–24 months = 10%.
- Remediation credit: explicit dual-cap model — up to 25% of platform fee per quarter for recurring SLA issues OR up to 20% of monthly managed services charges per incident, whichever is lower; full table will be in SOW.
- Engineering retainer: fixed-price 6-month retainer offered at $72,000 (covers up to 240 hours of engineering time allocated to rollout and runbook handoff). If additional hours required, we’ll bill at the agreed below-market uplift rate.
- Commercial validity: we will honor these numbers through 2026-06-30 provided a signed SOW or a binding PO is received.

Attachments: I will upload a tracked-change SOW and the pricing workbook with a pre-filled amortization tab for your $450k example by end of day. Links: HubSpot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DEAL-4721) and the DocuSign envelope placeholder (https://www.docusign.com/en/track?envelopeId=ABC-123-DEF).

Next steps: Amber/procurement — if the escape-credit bands and fixed retainer are acceptable, confirm and we’ll circulate a tracked SOW for redlines. Otherwise propose final bands and we’ll iterate.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
VP, Sales (Private Deployments)
Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_vpc_pricing_0519.xlsx (XLSX, 86KB); SOW_draft_v3.pdf (PDF, 248KB)
